title: affinity-driven-slab-rebalancer-and-write-through-reservation-for-paged-kv
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Introduces an affinity-driven slab rebalancer with a write-through reservation window and soft handoff to improve locality and reduce allocation latency. Lowers 99th percentile token latency under mixed workloads; no API changes.
description: Summary: Adds an affinity-driven slab rebalancer and a small write-through reservation window to the paged KV block allocator. Motivation: mixed inference workloads with varying sequence-length distributions revealed pathological allocation churn and cross-stream cache pollution. This resulted in elevated 95/99p token latency and extra CUDA kernel contention during heavy batching. Goals: 1) Reduce allocation stalls under bursty concurrency, 2) Improve per-stream locality for KV cache reuse, 3) Avoid global pauses during slab compaction.

merge_outcome: Merged into main via squash. Rollout: feature gated under runtime.flags.kv_affinity_rebalancer (default enabled for beta). Gradual rollout to Dedicated clusters over two weeks with telemetry focused on 95/99p token latency and allocator stall counts.
notes: Design: affinity score combines recent-access locality, owner stream id fingerprint, and slab coldness. Scoring is lightweight (single 64-bit counter updates) to avoid extra atomics on the hot path.

Reservation window: short-lived write-through reservations (default 20ms) let in-flight streams hold a micro-reservation for contiguous KV blocks. This increases reuse for follow-up tokens without long-term fragmentation.

Soft handoff: when rebalancer moves blocks between slabs, it marks ranges read-only and lets existing owners finish using them before finalizing the migration, avoiding global stop-the-world compactions.
Scheduler integration: worker pool now exposes a fast path to prefetch allocator hints into local per-worker alloc caches to reduce contention at high concurrency.
Safety: added invariants and sanitizers that run in debug builds to catch double-free or stale-KV access during handoffs.

Performance: benchmark results (mixed short+long sequences, 128 concurrent streams) show 12% lower 95p token latency and 18% fewer allocation stalls on p4d. Memory overhead increase is <1.8% due to short reservations and per-worker caches.
Testing: microbench harness covers reuse ratio, reservation expiration, and soft handoff correctness. Added integration test that replays a real customer trace to validate end-to-end behavior.

Risk: under extremely skewed workloads reservation windows could temporarily hold hot blocks; mitigated by per-slab cap and decay policy. Monitoring added to alert if reservation hold ratio exceeds 15% for longer than 5 minutes.
Rollback: feature flag and safe path to disable rebalancer without restart; disabling drains reservations and restores previous allocator policy immediately.
Related: ties into ENG-6732 (allocator stability) and ENG-6870 (kv-cache telemetry).
